---
title: "`r paste('PopPK Model Diagnostics -', basename(params$model_dir))`"
date: "`r format(Sys.time(), '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')`"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_float: false
    code_folding: hide
    number_sections: true
    css: style80p.css
params:
  # MANDATORY : Monolix output folder (e.g. "C:/Users/.../mymodel) - Don't forget to save ChartsData
  model_dir: "C:/Users/..." 
  # Optional: change to TRUE to save outputs in addition to knitted report (saved in output_dir)
  save_output: FALSE  
  # Optional: directory where outputs are saved (when save_output is TRUE), defaults to model_dir (set to "" for default)
  output_dir: "" 
  # Optional: prefix for saved output names, defaults to the model folder name (set to "" for default)
  prefix: ""
  # Optional: results of a convergence assessment, i.e. the object returned by lixoftConnectors::getAssessmentResults()
  # (or the path of an .rds file holding it). NULL (default) leaves the section out
  assessment: null
editor_options: 
  chunk_output_type: console
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = TRUE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5, fig.align = "center",
                      out.width = "90%")

# Optional analyses that did not run leave NULL objects: printing them would show "NULL" in the report
show_if <- function(x) if (is.null(x)) invisible(NULL) else x

# Runs a chunk's content and prints a short note instead of stopping the
# whole report if it errors -- used for sections that don't apply to every
# model (e.g. a structural-only model with no covariate tests at all, or a
# fully fixed model with no Fisher information matrix to show).
safe_run <- function(expr, label) {
  tryCatch(expr, error = function(e) {
    cat("*", label, "not available for this model:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
    invisible(NULL)
  })
}
```

# Run configuration 

This is the only section you should normally need to edit between runs -- either directly in the chunk below, or by passing the same values to `rmarkdown::render(params = list(...))` instead (see `model_checkup_auto.R`).

```{r run-config}
# Accepts a Windows-style path pasted with backslashes ("C:\...\model") and
# converts it to the forward-slash form R expects, noting when it does so.
normalize_path <- function(path, label) {
  if (!nzchar(path)) return(path)
  normalized <- gsub("\\\\", "/", path)
  if (!identical(normalized, path)) {
    message("Note: ", label, " contained backslashes; converted to: ", normalized)
  }
  normalized
}

# ---- Required ----------------------------------------------------------------
model_dir <- normalize_path(params$model_dir, "model_dir")

# ---- Optional -------------------------------------------------------------
output_dir <- normalize_path(params$output_dir, "output_dir")   # where saved outputs go
prefix     <- params$prefix                                    # filename prefix for saved outputs

if (!nzchar(model_dir)) {
  stop("model_dir is required -- set params$model_dir in the YAML header above, ",
      "or pass rmarkdown::render(params = list(model_dir = \"...\")).")
}
if (!dir.exists(model_dir)) stop("model_dir does not exist: ", model_dir)

model_name <- basename(model_dir)
if (!nzchar(output_dir)) output_dir <- model_dir
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)
if (!nzchar(prefix)) prefix <- model_name

# Save the outputs below to output_dir? Flip params$save_output to TRUE
# (directly here, in the YAML above, or from model_checkup_auto.R) --
# see "Save outputs" at the very end.
SAVE_OUTPUTS <- params$save_output

# Optional convergence assessment (the section is left out when nothing is provided)
has_assessment <- !is.null(params$assessment)
p_assessment_iterations <- NULL
p_assessment_estimates  <- NULL
```

```{r load-functions}
library(mlxflow)
# Used directly by the chunks below (installed together with mlxflow)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)
library(kableExtra)

```

```{r run-config-table, echo=FALSE}
tibble(
  Setting = c("Model", "Model folder", "Saved outputs", "Output folder", "File prefix", "Convergence assessment"),
  Value   = c(model_name, model_dir, ifelse(SAVE_OUTPUTS, "yes", "no (knitted report only)"),
              ifelse(SAVE_OUTPUTS, output_dir, "-"), ifelse(SAVE_OUTPUTS, prefix, "-"),
              ifelse(has_assessment, "provided", "not provided"))
) |>
  kable(booktabs = TRUE, caption = "Run configuration") |>
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, font_size = 12, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover")) |>
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE)
```

```{r check-chartsdata}
# Stops the run right away, with an explanation, if ChartsData is missing or
# empty -- nothing below can be built without it.
check_chartsdata(model_dir)
```

```{r resolve-dv}
# Resolved ONCE here and passed explicitly to every function below that
# takes a dv= argument -- avoids re-parsing .mlxtran (and re-triggering its
# "Several .mlxtran files found" warning, if applicable) on every single
# plot/table call in this report. The name is checked against the exported
# ChartsData file names (the ground truth), so a dataset column called "dv"
# whose observation is named e.g. "concentration" is handled. Edit dv_name
# below to force another one.
dv_name <- resolve_dv(model_dir)
```

```{r figure-sizes, include=FALSE}
# A handful of figures scale with model complexity (number of parameters,
# number of routes/strata) -- their height is computed here from the
# underlying data, rather than fixed, so they stay legible whether the
# model is a simple single-route PK model or a more complex one. Each is
# capped so a very complex model doesn't produce an unreasonably tall
# figure; adjust the cap (the first argument to min()) if you need more
# room for a given model.
conv_n_params <- n_distinct(read_convergence(model_dir)$parameter)
conv_height   <- min(12, max(5, 1.6 * ceiling(conv_n_params / 4)))

iparam_density  <- read_iparam_pdf(model_dir)$density
iparam_n_params <- length(unique(str_remove(colnames(iparam_density)[str_ends(colnames(iparam_density), "_abscissa")], "_abscissa$")))
iparam_height   <- min(12, max(5, 2.2 * ceiling(iparam_n_params / 3)))
```

# Estimation diagnostics 
## Population parameters 

```{r pop-params}
model_summary <- read_summary(file.path(model_dir, "summary.txt"), full = TRUE)
param_table   <- build_param_table(model_summary) |> clean_param_labels(overwrite = TRUE)

t_param_table <- kable_param_table(param_table, caption = paste("Population parameters -", model_name)) |> 
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, font_size = 11, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "bordered", "hover", "condensed")) |>
  kableExtra::footnote(symbol = c("Conditional distribution"))
t_param_table
```

## Fisher information matrix 

```{r fisher-matrix, fig.height=6}
p_fisher <- safe_run(plot_fisher_matrix(model_summary), "Fisher information matrix")
show_if(p_fisher)
```

## SAEM convergence 

```{r convergence, fig.height=conv_height}
p_convergence <- plot_convergence(model_dir)
p_convergence
```

```{r convergence-assessment, results="asis", echo=FALSE, eval=has_assessment, fig.height=5}
# Optional: only shown when `assessment` is provided (see the YAML above)
cat("## Convergence assessment\n\n")
cat("SAEM was run several times from different initial values: the curves of the runs should end on the same values.\n\n")
p_assessment_iterations <- safe_run(plot_convergence_assessment(params$assessment, which = "iterations"), "Convergence assessment (iterations)")
if (!is.null(p_assessment_iterations)) print(p_assessment_iterations)
cat("\n\n")
p_assessment_estimates <- safe_run(plot_convergence_assessment(params$assessment, which = "estimates"), "Convergence assessment (final estimates)")
if (!is.null(p_assessment_estimates)) print(p_assessment_estimates)
```

## Individual parameter distributions (shrinkage) 

```{r iparam-distributions, fig.height=iparam_height}
p_iparam_distributions <- plot_iparam_distribution(model_dir)
p_iparam_distributions
```

## Covariate assessment 

Random-effect x covariate correlation (covariate search) -- the heatmap below and the table underneath it show the same `Tests/correlationRandomEffectsCovariates.txt` data, just rendered two ways; the table is kept (for saving) but not printed here since it's large and mostly redundant with the heatmap. Pass `covariates = c(...)` to either `plot_covariate_search()` or `covariate_tests_table()` to restrict both to a handful of covariates of interest (case-insensitive substring match, e.g. `"WT"` also matches `"logtWT"`).

```{r covariate-search-plot, fig.height=5, fig.width=10}
p_covariate_search <- safe_run(plot_covariate_search(model_dir), "Covariate search heatmap")
show_if(p_covariate_search)
```

```{r covariate-search-table}
t_covariate_search <- safe_run(covariate_tests_table(model_dir, which = "search"), "Covariate search table")
# t_covariate_search
```

Confirmation tests for covariate effects already in the model (correlation test + Wald test):

```{r covariate-confirmation-tables}
t_covariate_confirmation <- safe_run(covariate_tests_table(model_dir, which = "confirmation"), "Covariate confirmation table")
show_if(t_covariate_confirmation)

t_covariate_wald <- safe_run(covariate_tests_table(model_dir, which = "wald"), "Covariate Wald test table")
show_if(t_covariate_wald)
```

# Predictive performance 
## Observed vs Predicted 

split = TRUE below shows population/individual panels per route -- worth keeping on for a model with a meaningful route split, since it's more informative than pooling routes together; it's no longer required just to keep Monolix's own smoother from overlaying mismatched routes in a single panel (that mismatch is now detected automatically and falls back to a freshly fit smoother instead, whichever way split is set).

```{r obspred, fig.width=6}
# Size levers for this figure (same for every chunk in this report):
#  - fig.width / fig.height (chunk options, inches): shape of the image and the
#    text-to-plot proportions (text size is fixed in points, so a larger
#    fig.width makes text relatively smaller); base_size= below sets text size.
#  - out.width (chunk option, set to 90% for all chunks in `setup`): how wide the
#    image is DISPLAYED in the html, whatever fig.width is -- e.g. add
#    out.width = "60%" to the chunk header to make this figure smaller on screen.
obspred_res <- obspred_diagnostics(model_dir, dv = dv_name, split = TRUE)
# obspred_res$data / $metrics / $obspred / $aipe

p_obspred <- obspred_res$obspred
p_obspred
```

## Absolute individual prediction error 

```{r aipe}
p_aipe <- obspred_res$aipe
p_aipe
```

## Metrics table 

```{r metrics-table}
metrics_display <- obspred_res$metrics |> select(-Prediction)   # packed via auto_pack_rows below instead

t_metrics <- metrics_display |>
  kable(booktabs = TRUE, caption = paste("Prediction-error metrics -", model_name)) |>
  auto_pack_rows(obspred_res$metrics, "Prediction") |>
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, font_size = 12, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "bordered", "hover")) |>
  style_metrics_table(metrics_display)
t_metrics
```

## Visual predictive check 

facet_scales = "free" below lets both axes adjust per route/stratum panel (concentration ranges can differ a lot between e.g. an oral and an IM route); pass facet_scales = "free_x" (the function's own default, kept mainly for comparing percentile levels side by side) or "fixed" instead if that's not what you want for a given model.

```{r vpc, fig.height=5}
# show_observations = TRUE adds the raw observations (grey) to the VPC
p_vpc <- plot_vpc(model_dir, dv = dv_name, facet_scales = "free", show_observations = TRUE)
p_vpc
```

```{r npde-time, fig.height=5}

p_npde_time
```

p_npde_predictions <- plot_npde(model_dir, dv = dv_name, type = "predictions")
p_npde_predictions
```

```

# Structure & covariate effects 

Once the diagnostics above are satisfactory, here is what the covariate effects already in the model actually look like.

```{r covariate-effects}
covariate_effects_res <- safe_run(compute_covariate_effects(model_dir), "Covariate effects")

t_covariate_effects          <- NULL
p_covariate_effects          <- NULL   # named list, one panel per PK parameter (for individual saving)
p_covariate_effects_combined <- NULL   # every parameter combined into one figure
covfx_height                 <- 4

if (!is.null(covariate_effects_res)) {

  t_covariate_effects <- covariate_effects_res$table |>
    mutate(Param_value = round(Param_value, 4)) |>
    kable(booktabs  = TRUE,
         col.names = c("Parameter", "Covariate", "Relationship", "Type", "Level", "Value", "Relative change (%)"),
         caption   = sprintf("Relative effect of model's covariates \u2014 %s", model_name)) |>
    kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, font_size = 11, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover")) |>
    auto_pack_rows(covariate_effects_res$table, group_vars = c("Relationship", "Parameter")) |>
    column_spec(
      which(names(covariate_effects_res$table) == "Relative_change_pct"),
      bold  = covariate_effects_res$table$Relative_change_pct != 0 & abs(covariate_effects_res$table$Relative_change_pct) > 20,
      color = case_when(
        covariate_effects_res$table$Relative_change_pct != 0 & abs(covariate_effects_res$table$Relative_change_pct) < 20 ~ "firebrick",
        TRUE ~ "grey30"
      )
    ) |>
    column_spec(1, italic = TRUE) |>
    remove_column(c(1, 3))

  p_covariate_effects          <- covariate_effects_res$plots
  p_covariate_effects_combined <- combine_all_plots(covariate_effects_res)
  covfx_height <- min(14, max(6, 4 * ceiling(length(covariate_effects_res$plots_flat) / 3)))
}

show_if(t_covariate_effects)
```

```{r covariate-effects-plot, fig.height=covfx_height, eval=!is.null(p_covariate_effects_combined)}
p_covariate_effects_combined
```

# Save outputs 

Flip `save_output` to `TRUE` in the params above (or from `model_checkup_auto.R`, then re-knit) to write the files below to `output_dir`. Every file name starts with `prefix`, so outputs from different models never collide in the same folder.

```{r save-plots, eval=SAVE_OUTPUTS}
save_plot <- function(plot, suffix, width = 8, height = 6) {
  if (is.null(plot)) return(invisible(NULL))
  ggsave(filename = file.path(output_dir, paste0(prefix, "_", suffix, ".png")),
        plot = plot, width = width, height = height, dpi = 320)
}

save_plot(p_fisher, "fisher_matrix")
save_plot(p_convergence, "convergence", height = conv_height)
save_plot(p_assessment_iterations, "convergence_assessment_iterations", height = 5)
save_plot(p_assessment_estimates, "convergence_assessment_estimates", height = 5)
save_plot(p_iparam_distributions, "iparam_distributions", height = iparam_height)
save_plot(p_covariate_search, "covariate_search", height = 5)
save_plot(p_obspred, "obspred", height = 8)
save_plot(p_aipe, "aipe")
save_plot(p_vpc, "vpc", height = 5)
save_plot(p_npde_time, "npde_time", height = 5)
save_plot(p_npde_predictions, "npde_predictions", height = 5)
save_plot(p_npde_density, "npde_density", height = 5)
save_plot(p_npde_qq, "npde_qq", height = 5)
save_plot(p_covariate_effects_combined, "covariate_effects_combined", width = 14, height = covfx_height)
if (!is.null(p_covariate_effects)) {
  for (nm in names(p_covariate_effects)) {
    save_plot(p_covariate_effects[[nm]], paste0("covariate_effect_", nm), height = 6)
  }
}

cat("Plots saved to:", output_dir, "\n")
```

```{r save-tables, eval=SAVE_OUTPUTS}
# Tables are saved as standalone HTML (self-contained, no extra system
# dependency). PNG export is also possible via save_kable(..., file = "*.png")
# but additionally requires the webshot2 package (plus a headless browser).
save_table <- function(kbl, suffix) {
  if (is.null(kbl)) return(invisible(NULL))
  save_kable(kbl, file.path(output_dir, paste0(prefix, "_", suffix, ".html")))
}

save_table(t_param_table, "param_table")
save_table(t_covariate_search, "covariate_search_table")
save_table(t_covariate_confirmation, "covariate_confirmation_table")
save_table(t_covariate_wald, "covariate_wald_table")
save_table(t_metrics, "metrics_table")
save_table(t_covariate_effects, "covariate_effects_table")

write.csv(obspred_res$metrics, file.path(output_dir, paste0(prefix, "_metrics.csv")), row.names = FALSE)
if (!is.null(covariate_effects_res)) {
  write.csv(covariate_effects_res$table, file.path(output_dir, paste0(prefix, "_covariate_effects.csv")), row.names = FALSE)
}

cat("Tables saved to:", output_dir, "\n")
```

```{r save-rdata, eval=SAVE_OUTPUTS}
saveRDS(
  list(obspred = obspred_res, covariate_effects = covariate_effects_res, summary = model_summary),
  file = file.path(output_dir, paste0(prefix, "_diagnostics.rds"))
)

cat("Done --", model_name, "diagnostics complete.\n")
```


Instead of pressing the Knit button in RStudio, you can execute an R command.  
Using Knit button will generates model_checkup.html in working directory by default.  
The command let you rename the html output (e.g. with the prefix) and change is location (e.g. in output_dir).  
-> See model_checkup_auto.R
